newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH REFINER UNIPETROL PLANS SHARE SWAP RATIO.
newsitem.headline: CZECH REFINER UNIPETROL PLANS SHARE SWAP RATIO.

text.p: The boards of shareholders comprising the main Czech refining company Unipetrol a.s. on Wednesday announced their plan for the conversion of Kaucuk a.s. and Chemopetrol a.s. shares into Unipetrol shares.

In a joint statement of the boards of Chemopetrol, Kaucuk and Unipetrol, the boards said they agreed to swap one Chemopetrol share for between 1.05 to 1.20 Unipetrol shares, and one Kaucuk share for between 1.10 to 1.25 Unipetrol shares.
It said the plan had been agreed at a meeting on Tuesday between the members of the respective boards, but that final approval must come from general meetings of each companies' shareholders.

Investors have been eagerly awaiting the ratio announcement, as Kaucuk and Chemopetrol shares have been virtually equal for months on the Prague equities markets, following the cleaving of the two companies refinery operations into Unipetrol at the end of 1995.

Ahead of the news on Wednesday, Kaucuk shares were fixed 11 crowns above Tuesday's close on the Prague Stock Exchange at 1,105, while Chemopetrol finished the PSE's Wednesday continuous trading session 12 crowns higher at 1,106.
"The state of preparation at this moment allows to estimate the intervals in which the proposed conversion ratio of shares of the dormant companies would most probably range," the statement said.

"The current results of appraising the assets and liabilities of the involved companies, which will be the basis for determining the conversion ratio, are leading us to publishing the given intervals...," it said.

Under a complicated privatisation of the Czech petrochemical industry, Kaucuk and Chemopetrol's refining operations were merged into a subsidiary of the newly-created Unipetrol last year called Ceska Rafinerska a.s..
Unipetrol, in which the government currently holds a 100 percent stake, has a 51 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska,

The IOC consortium -- comprising U.S. Du Pont de Nemours unit Conoco, Royal Dutch/Shell , and Italy's Agip SpA [AGIS.CN] -- acquired a 49 percent stake in Rafinerska under agreement with the government last year.

The share swap would complete the transfer of the rest of Kaucuk and Chemopetrol as subsidiaries under Unipetrol, which acts as a holding company, and would dilute the state's 100 percent stake in Unipetrol.
